_comment: autoDQM isolation-forest pipeline — central configuration. All paths are absolute so the file works from Condor worker nodes, cron jobs, or any working directory. CLI arguments always override these values.
_comment_input: Run lists: text files where each line is a glob pattern resolving to Digitizer CSV files. data_path is the base directory; the individual lists are absolute paths derived from it.
_comment_output: model_tag namespaces all outputs: models/<tag>/, logs/<tag>.csv, reports/<tag>/, plots/<tag>/.
_comment_features: Feature set flags. use_trigger includes TriggerBoard rate features; use_lvds includes LVDS pin-count features. ignore_features is a list of glob patterns for features to exclude entirely from training and scoring (e.g. 'TDCRollovers_*' drops TDCRollovers_mean/std/median).
_comment_thresholds: Detection: z_threshold is the |z-score| above which a feature is flagged; if_contamination is the expected anomaly fraction for IsolationForest. --- Persistence-based alert (sustained degradation): file_alert_n_channels is the minimum number of *persistent* anomalous channels for [ALERT] — can be low (e.g. 2) because persistence already suppresses transient noise; alert_consecutive_n is how many consecutive files a channel must be anomalous in to count as persistent (1 = disabled). --- Single-file severity alerts (no persistence required, fire on one bad file): single_file_alert_n_channels triggers [ALERT] when this many channels are anomalous at once — targets sudden widespread events like a power glitch; set higher than file_alert_n_channels (e.g. 5) since there is no persistence filter; 0 = disabled. single_file_alert_max_z triggers [ALERT] when any channel's max_z reaches this value — targets a single catastrophically out-of-range channel (e.g. broken hardware); 0.0 = disabled.
_comment_misc: poll_interval: seconds between directory scans in watch mode. test_seed: random seed for reproducible test-mode file sampling. max_subrun_plots: per category, produce up to this many subrun plot sets — max_subrun_plots random bad subruns (always including the worst) and max_subrun_plots random good subruns (below file_alert_n_channels). -1 = no limit (plots every file — can be very slow and disk-heavy; a loud warning is printed).
